svg.title: SURMOUNT-MAINTAIN: stepping tirzepatide down to 5 mg kept most, not all, of the weight off
svg.desc: Stayed on 10 or 15 mg: weight -21.9% from start at week 112, 11 of 138 (8%) needed rescue tirzepatide; Dropped to 5 mg: weight -16.6% from start at week 112, 35 of 142 (25%) needed rescue tirzepatide; Switched to placebo: weight -9.9% from start at week 112, 60 of 90 (67%) needed rescue tirzepatide. 378 people randomized at week 60 after reaching their maximum tolerated dose. Funded by Eli Lilly.

text.font-family: Inter, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The best test of a lower dose: half-way, not micro

svg.text: 5 mg is Zepbound’s lowest maintenance dose: a third to a half of what these people had been taking, and at

text.font-family: Inter, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: least 4 times the “microdose” range (25–50% of 2.5 mg). One in four on 5 mg still regained enough to need rescue.

text.font-family: Inter, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Rescue was allowed from week 84. Funded by Eli Lilly; several authors are Lilly employees.
